Continuing a Score-Driven Filter Past the Series

Source: R/gas.R
term_continue.GasTerm.Rd

Computes the level that the recursion reaches at rows that come after the observed ones.

Arguments

term

A built score-driven term.

psi

The term's parameters, named as term_params().

f_past

The level at each observed row.

s_past

The score at each observed row.

newdata

The rows onto which to continue, carrying the variables that by and time name.

...

Ignored.

deriv

NULL, or a list giving the derivatives of the inputs in a vector of m coordinates of the caller's choosing: df_past and ds_past, one row per observed row and m columns, the derivatives of f_past and s_past; and dpsi, length(psi) rows and m columns, the derivative of psi. The continuation is then differentiated along with its value, by the same recursion run on derivative rows, because the score past the data and its derivative are zero.

Value

A numeric vector of nrow(newdata) levels. With deriv, it carries the attribute "jacobian", a nrow(newdata) by m matrix: the derivative of each level in the caller's coordinates.

Details

The recursion is the filter's own, started from the levels and scores of the observed part. A lag that falls before the first observed row of a group takes the first observed level, which equals the starting level. Past the data the score is the quantity that changes: it has zero conditional mean by construction, the model's own defining property, so at a row whose response is not observed the driving term is its expectation and the continuation is the deterministic recursion $$f_{n+h} = \omega + \sum_i \kappa_i s_{n+h-i} + \sum_j \xi_j f_{n+h-j},$$ where the loadings contribute only while \(n+h-i\) is still an observed time. The continuation involves no simulation and no integration.

The new rows of a group are ordered by their own time and must come after every observed time of that group. The continuation treats them as consecutive steps whatever the spacing of the times, so that a gap between two times counts as one step, as in the sample. A row that falls inside the series belongs to the observed data, where the response is known, so the filter must be run on it and not continued; such a row is rejected, and the rows are named. A group that was not in the data of the fit is rejected for the same reason: there is no state to continue. The term must have been built with time.

See also

term_continue(), term_filter()
